oleleh-sl.description: A vegetarian Oleleh adaptation: black-eyed bean pudding cooked by covered water-bath steaming.
oleleh-sl.story: Based on Isata’s vegetarian preparation published by Healthy Living Platform. It uses vegetables instead of fish.
oleleh-sl.regional_variations: Pamela Greene’s Sierra Leone recipe uses fish and palm oil and steams portions in wrappers or containers.
oleleh-sl.occasion: Serve as a savoury snack or alongside a meal.
oleleh-sl.review_summary: Replaces the generic frying template with a named cook’s steamed vegetarian version. Active preparation estimate excludes overnight soaking; doneness governs cooking time. Nutrition has not been calculated for this version.
oleleh-sl.official_source_status: Culinary sources, not government guidance. No kitchen test performed by AfroTools.

sources.title: Healthy Living Platform: Olehleh by Isata
West Africa Cooks: Oleleh, from Pamela Greene

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.prep_note: for blending; additional water for soaking and the water bath

steps.title: Prepare beans
steps.instruction: Soak the dried beans overnight, then drain and remove their skins.

steps.title: Blend
steps.instruction: Blend beans with water, onion, garlic, salt, oil and half of each pepper until smooth.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.instruction: Finely chop the remaining peppers and mix them into the batter with the carrot.

steps.title: Prepare water bath
steps.instruction: Heat the fan oven to 200°C. Fill greased small baking containers with batter, cover with foil and stand them in a larger tray of water.

steps.title: Steam
steps.instruction: Cook for about 40 minutes, until firm and a testing knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Lift containers carefully from the hot water and serve warm.

oleleh-sl.image_alt: Illustration of steamed vegetarian Oleleh bean puddings with finely chopped peppers and carrot.

ladob-sc.name: Ladob Patat
ladob-sc.description: Seychellois sweet potatoes gently simmered in coconut milk with vanilla and nutmeg.
ladob-sc.story: This version follows the sweet-potato preparation published by Jean-Paul and Marie-Celice at The Creole Melting Pot.
ladob-sc.regional_variations: Ladob also includes plantain and breadfruit desserts; this recipe specifies sweet potato.
ladob-sc.best_served_with: Serve on its own, warm or cold.
ladob-sc.review_summary: Replaces generic binder and bake/steam/fry instructions. Timing follows the source method (about 40 minutes), not its30-minute header. No kitchen test or nutrition calculation by AfroTools.
ladob-sc.official_source_status: Named cooks supply the recipe; cultural reference supports dessert identity.

sources.title: The Creole Melting Pot: Sweet Potato Daube

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.prep_note: scrubbed; cut into roughly 3 cm pieces

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.prep_note: optional; add only if needed to cover the potatoes

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Scrub the sweet potatoes and cut into even chunks.

steps.title: Combine
steps.instruction: Put potatoes in a wide saucepan. Add coconut milk, vanilla, salt, nutmeg and sugar. Add water only if needed to cover the pieces.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.instruction: Bring to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer gently, uncovered, for about 40 minutes, until a knife enters the potatoes easily and the sauce is creamy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Remove the vanilla pod before serving warm or cold.

ladob-sc.image_alt: Tender sweet-potato chunks in creamy coconut sauce with vanilla and nutmeg; AI-generated Ladob Patat illustration

latchiri-kossan-gn.name: Latchiri Kossan
latchiri-kossan-gn.description: Steamed maize couscous served with cultured milk, in an adaptation of Guinean preparations.
latchiri-kossan-gn.story: The maize-and-milk identity is described by Guinean agronomist Sekouna Camara. This adaptation combines Dienaba Traore's granule preparation with the measured maize batch published under Youssouf Gassama's name.
latchiri-kossan-gn.regional_variations: Maize texture and steaming time vary. This version uses maize flour and ready-made cultured milk.
latchiri-kossan-gn.best_served_with: Ready-made cultured milk; sugar or salt to taste.
latchiri-kossan-gn.review_summary: Replaces the boiled-porridge template with steamed maize. The 1 kg maize quantity and 12 servings follow the attributed PDF. Thirty minutes preparation is an editorial planning estimate; steaming may need a further 15 minutes. Cultured milk is ready-made, not fermented using the PDF instructions. No AfroTools kitchen test or nutrition calculation.
latchiri-kossan-gn.official_source_status: Primary agronomic context plus culinary sources; the public PDF author's identity has not been independently verified.

sources.title: Latchiri Kossan, attributed to Youssouf Gassama
sources.source_type: public recipe document with author metadata

sources.title: FAO: Production et utilisation du mais en Guinee, Sekouna Camara

ingredients.name: maize flour
ingredients.prep_note: for steamed maize granules; not corn starch

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.prep_note: as needed for moistening and the steamer

steps.title: Form granules
steps.instruction: Sprinkle water gradually over the maize flour, rubbing it into fine, loose granules. Do not make a batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.instruction: Bring water to a boil below a couscous steamer. Line its upper basket with a clean, light steaming cloth and add the maize. Keep the maize above the water.

steps.title: First steaming
steps.instruction: Cover and steam for about 30 minutes. Transfer carefully to a bowl, loosen with a spoon and let it cool enough to handle.

steps.title: Moisten and loosen
steps.instruction: Sprinkle with a little water and salt to taste. Rest for 10 minutes, then separate the granules. Replenish the steamer water as needed.

steps.title: Steam again
steps.instruction: Steam for another 30 minutes, until soft. If still firm, loosen and steam for up to 15 minutes more, checking the water below.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Fluff the maize and serve with ready-made cultured milk. Add sugar or salt to taste.

latchiri-kossan-gn.image_alt: Illustration of steamed maize granules served with cultured milk for latchiri kossan.

kat-kat-banane-sc.name: Kat-Kat Banane
kat-kat-banane-sc.description: A savoury plantain and fish dish, adapted from The Creole Melting Pot's trevally katkat.
kat-kat-banane-sc.story: This page presents one attributed Seychellois preparation. AfroTools has not kitchen-tested the adaptation.
kat-kat-banane-sc.regional_variations: Other households use different fish or cooking bananas.
kat-kat-banane-sc.best_served_with: Rice or chilli sauce, if desired.
kat-kat-banane-sc.review_summary: Replaces generic stew directions. Source timings are planning values, not a tested guarantee. Nutrition is uncalculated; dietary certification is not asserted.

sources.title: The Creole Melting Pot: Trevally Katkat with Green Plantain (10 September 2019)
Africa-Europe Cook Book: Banana Kat Kat, attributed to EU Delegation to Mauritius and the Seychelles
supports: independent dish identity and mashed banana/fish/coconut preparation; different quantities and fish cooking sequence, not blended into this version

steps.title: Cook fish
steps.instruction: Season fish pieces. Boil gently until cooked, about 10 minutes. Reserve the liquid; cool, check for bones and flake.

steps.title: Cook plantains
steps.instruction: Trim and halve the washed, unpeeled plantains. Boil separately until tender, about 15 minutes. Cool enough to handle, peel and roughly mash.

steps.title: Combine
steps.instruction: Warm the mash with coconut milk. Add fish and cinnamon; simmer 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently. Loosen with reserved fish liquid if needed.

steps.title: Finish
steps.instruction: Remove cinnamon, adjust seasoning and serve. Keep a thick, coarse texture with visible fish pieces.

kat-kat-banane-sc.image_alt: Illustration of roughly mashed plantain with flaked fish in a creamy coconut mixture.

nthochi-bread-mw.name: Nthochi Bread
nthochi-bread-mw.description: A baked banana loaf using Christian Aid Ireland's published Malawian recipe.
nthochi-bread-mw.story: This version follows Christian Aid Ireland's October 2022 recipe. Other bakers use different ingredients and timings.
nthochi-bread-mw.regional_variations: This page presents one attributed version, not a universal formula.
nthochi-bread-mw.review_summary: Replaces an ambiguous template with an attributed baked loaf. The source gives 8-12 servings; 10 slices is the editorial scaling default. Prep15 is an estimate; bake30-45 uses45 for planning. Cooling is additional. Not kitchen-tested by AfroTools; nutrition is uncalculated.
nthochi-bread-mw.official_source_status: Published charity recipe; not a government or nutritional authority.

sources.title: Christian Aid Ireland: Malawian banana bread (October 2022)
Together Women Rise: Nthochi Bread, Georgia Reader
supports: independent baked banana loaf identity; different formula, not used for quantities or timings

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Grease or line a 2 lb loaf tin; mash the bananas.

steps.title: Mix wet ingredients
steps.instruction: Cream butter with sugar until fluffy. Gently mix in eggs, then banana.

steps.title: Finish batter
steps.instruction: Fold in flour and baking powder. Transfer the batter to the tin.

steps.title: Bake and check
steps.instruction: Bake for 30 minutes. Test the centre with a skewer; if wet batter remains, bake in 5-minute intervals and retest. The source allows up to 45 minutes.

steps.title: Cool
steps.instruction: Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool before slicing.

nthochi-bread-mw.image_alt: Illustration of sliced Nthochi banana bread.

mandazi-tanzania-tz.name: Tanzanian Mandazi
mandazi-tanzania-tz.description: Coconut and cardamom fried bread, adapted from Miriam Malaquias's Maandazi recipe.
mandazi-tanzania-tz.story: An attributed household version; AfroTools has not kitchen-tested this adaptation.
mandazi-tanzania-tz.regional_variations: Shapes and doughs vary; this version uses round cutters.
mandazi-tanzania-tz.review_summary: Adds the missing yeast and complete dough sequence. Source recommends starting 90 minutes ahead; 75 preparation and 15 frying minutes are editorial planning allocations, not measured source timings. Rising depends on conditions; follow the doubling cue. Nutrition uncalculated; no dietary certification asserted.

sources.title: QASA QASA: Mandazi Recipe, updated 18 April 2022
supports: independent coconut-cardamom yeast-dough identity and variable rising time; different quantities and triangular shaping are not combined with this version

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.prep_note: plus a little for adjustments and the work surface

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.prep_note: increase up to 4 tablespoons if desired

ingredients.name: coconut milk
ingredients.prep_note: start with two-thirds; reserve the rest

steps.title: Activate yeast
steps.instruction: Combine warm water, starter sugar and yeast. Cover until visibly active.

steps.title: Make dough
steps.instruction: Add remaining sugar, cardamom, optional oil and two-thirds of the coconut milk. Work in flour. Adjust a stiff dough with reserved coconut milk; add small amounts of flour if sticky.

steps.title: Knead and rise
steps.instruction: Knead for 10 minutes. Cover in a lightly oiled bowl until doubled; use the volume change rather than a fixed timer.

steps.title: Shape
steps.instruction: Knead again for 2 minutes. Roll to approximately 5 mm and cut rounds.

steps.title: Fry
steps.instruction: Deep-fry in vegetable oil until golden. Serve warm or at room temperature.

mandazi-tanzania-tz.image_alt: Illustration of plain round golden mandazi, with one opened to show an airy bread-like interior.

mchemsho-tz.name: Mchemsho — beef and vegetables
mchemsho-tz.description: A beef version of TaTEDO’s electric-pressure-cooker Mchemsho, with potatoes and vegetables in broth.
mchemsho-tz.story: Adapted from the Tanzania eCookbook (TaTEDO, 2020), printed pages 38–39. This version selects beef and omits the optional additions. It has not been kitchen-tested by AfroTools.
mchemsho-tz.regional_variations: This page documents one attributed pressure-cooker version; it does not describe every household’s Mchemsho.
mchemsho-tz.best_served_with: Serve the vegetables and beef with their broth.

steps.title: Prepare the cooker
steps.instruction: Check the manufacturer’s capacity and minimum-liquid instructions. Use a suitable cooker or scale the whole recipe down; never exceed its fill limit.

steps.title: Cook the beef
steps.instruction: Add beef and water. Pressure-cook for 20 minutes using your appliance instructions.
steps.timer_label: pressure-cooking stage; excludes heat-up and release

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.instruction: Depressurize safely before opening. Add the prepared vegetables and salt; check liquid and fill limits, then pressure-cook for 7 minutes.
steps.timer_label: pressure-cooking stage; excludes heat-up and release

steps.title: Check and serve
steps.instruction: Release pressure as instructed by the appliance maker. Check that the beef is cooked and tender; continue cooking if needed, then serve hot.

ndizi-nyama-tz.name: Ndizi na Nyama
ndizi-nyama-tz.description: Beef and green plantains in a tomato-coconut stew.
ndizi-nyama-tz.story: Adapted from Darlene’s International Cuisine recipe. AfroTools has not kitchen-tested this version.
ndizi-nyama-tz.regional_variations: This documents one attributed version. Do not treat different household recipes as interchangeable.

steps.title: Start the stew
steps.instruction: Soften onion and garlic in oil over medium heat. Add beef and brown its surfaces.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.instruction: Stir in carrot, tomatoes, water and seasoning; cover and bring to a boil.

steps.title: Cook plantains
steps.instruction: Add plantains and cook for about 10 minutes.
steps.timer_label: check texture and doneness; continue if needed

steps.title: Finish gently
steps.instruction: Stir in coconut milk and simmer for about 5 minutes. Continue as needed until the beef is cooked and tender and plantains yield to a fork. Add cilantro before serving.
steps.timer_label: check texture and doneness; continue if needed

kapenta-stew-zm.name: Kapenta Stew
kapenta-stew-zm.description: Dried small fish with onion, tomato and curry seasoning, adapted from Zambian Kitchen.
kapenta-stew-zm.story: An attributed Zambian preparation. AfroTools has not kitchen-tested this adaptation.
kapenta-stew-zm.regional_variations: This page follows one Zambian Kitchen method, not every regional version.

ingredients.name: cooking oil
ingredients.prep_note: as needed for frying; source gives no fixed amount

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.prep_note: enough for soaking, plus a small splash for the sauce

steps.title: Toast briefly
steps.instruction: Stir the sorted fish in a dry pan for about 5 minutes without burning.

steps.title: Soak and dry
steps.instruction: Cover with cold water for about 5 minutes. Drain and pat thoroughly dry before frying.

steps.title: Fry the fish
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pan. Fry the fish, stirring, for about 5 minutes and until browned.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.instruction: Stir in onion and curry powder; cook for about a minute.

steps.title: Soften the tomato
steps.instruction: Add tomato, cover and cook gently for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.instruction: Add a small splash of water and simmer, covered, for about 3 minutes; check that everything is cooked before serving.

kapenta-stew-zm.review_summary: The source lists2cups fish in ingredients and250g in its method; this adaptation uses the explicitly stated mass without claiming a cup conversion. Oil and water remain unmeasured as in the source. Four servings and10/25/35minute planning times are editorial estimates. This does not borrow Zimbabwean ingredient quantities or imply kitchen testing.
kapenta-stew-zm.official_source_status: Attributed cooking sources, not regulatory certification.
kapenta-stew-zm.confidence: Source-backed editorial adaptation; unmeasured ingredients and planning estimates disclosed.
